content.overview: An agreement to do an act impossible in itself is void. A contract becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful after formation by reason of an event the promisor could not prevent. Commercial hardship alone is not frustration.

sections.heading: Doctrine
sections.body: Section 56 codifies frustration. Satyabrata Ghose v. Mugneeram Bangur orients the doctrine toward practical impossibility of the contemplated performance. Energy Watchdog v. CERC cautions that commercial unprofitability is not frustration.

sections.heading: Restitution
sections.body: Section 65 requires restoration of advantage received under a void agreement or when a contract becomes void.

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: Plead the supervening event, lack of fault, and destruction of the contractual foundation. Force-majeure clauses may allocate risk differently from bare s. 56.
